title: Model the bridge to the text's wording
statement: When the words a lesson tells learners to search for differ from the text's own wording, model the link between them before asking learners to search.
detail: A case study of one Grade 3 reading lesson found that the lesson named one word as the search keyword while the passage expressed the same idea in a different phrase; the two had been treated as obviously equivalent, and learners were never shown that bridge before using the search term (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans-wiki/Peter-Pan-Quality-Case-Study-2026-08-24.md`, lines 312-316). The repair had the model connect the search language to the passage wording before asking the child to use it, and the durable rule is that when procedure language and source language differ the synonymy must be modelled, or the course hides a required operation inside assumed knowledge (same file, lines 318-322). The prevention it names is a review of each search term against its source span and a locate trace played as the learner (same file, line 324).
against: The evidence is one lesson's case study, which says it is not a standard and is no evidence about lessons not inspected (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans-wiki/Peter-Pan-Quality-Case-Study-2026-08-24.md`, lines 4-5).

evidence.quote: The learner had not been shown that semantic bridge before using the search term.
The model explicitly connected the search language to the passage wording before asking the child to use it.
When procedure language and source language differ, expert synonymy must be modelled. Otherwise the course hides a required operation inside assumed knowledge.
